parts.layout_phase: Rojdi C, 'possibly the early part of this period' (Possehl and Raval's ceramic phase)
parts.what_was_built: A circumvallation of large basalt boulders, set in shallow foundation trenches as a double line 1.5 to 2 m apart packed with rammed earth and rubble, which 'encloses the entire settlement, save for the river side', with a double-bastioned gateway on the west (possehl1989rojdi pp. 27-29). The gateway excavation showed that the circumvallation and gateway 'post-date the earliest Harappan occupation at Rojdi' (p. 29). The Large Square Building on the North Slope was built in the same architectural period, on the same hard black-soil surface (p. 29), and the excavators conclude that the Large Square Building, gateway and circumvallation 'were all built very close to one another in time and date to Rojdi C, possibly the early part of this period' (p. 140). The large building of Architectural Subphase 2b on the Main Mound, cut into the last Rojdi B stratum of trench 46L, opens Rojdi C, and all building on the South Extension is Rojdi C (p. 130); together these are 'the main architectural period' and 'were built near the end of the protohistoric occupation of the site' (p. 50). The boulder wall was first noticed in 1957-58, when the mound 'was scraped at several places and revealed the remains of a protection-wall made of big boulders' (IAR 1957-58, p. 18).
parts.excavator_basis: Ceramic correlation tied to radiocarbon. The pottery from the gateway and from the trenches joining the circumvallation and the Large Square Building is Rojdi C, with a few possibly late Rojdi B pieces from weathered near-surface strata (pp. 131, 140). Rojdi C is dated 2000-1700 B.C. as one of 'the basic dates for the ceramic phases', which combine the relative sequence with the calibrated radiocarbon dates of Tables 1-3 (p. 171). No radiocarbon sample comes from the wall itself.

syntheses.statement: Possehl and Raval's own synthesis: Rojdi A (2500-2200 B.C.) and Rojdi B (2200-2000 B.C.) are the 'Sorath Harappan', a regional expression of the Urban Phase, and Rojdi C (2000-1700 B.C.) has pottery 'characteristic of the early Post-urban'. The ranges rest on the calibrated PRL and TF dates.

Mandal notes that there is no C14 date for Phase A of the 1950s-60s excavations and doubts both Phase B dates: TF-199 from Pit 2 sealed by layer 4 is younger than TF-200 from layer 3 by about 225 years, which he calls 'real' at 95% confidence, and he concludes there is 'doubt about the validity of both dates'.
syntheses.disagreement: Rejects the only radiocarbon dates the earlier excavators had for the phase before the enclosure.

syntheses.statement: Kanungo and colleagues list fortifications 'around some settlements, including Kuntasi, Rojdi, and Pithad/Jaidak but none are close to what we get in Classic Harappan sites', reprint Possehl and Raval's Rojdi dates, and write that 'Rojdi-B has been dated by 14C to 2200-1900 BCE (Possehl and Raval 1989, 12)', following Dhavalikar and colleagues (1996: 32).
syntheses.disagreement: Ends Rojdi B at 1900 BCE where Possehl and Raval end it at 2000 B.C. (p. 171), which would move the start of Rojdi C, and so the enclosure, a century later.

parts.conflicts: Two excavation programmes use different phase schemes. P. P. Pandya (1957-59) and J. M. Nanavati (1962-63) divided Period I into Phases A, B and C (IAR 1958-59, pp. 19-20; IAR 1962-63, p. 8), while Possehl and Raval (1982-86) use the ceramic phases Rojdi A, B and C; we found no explicit concordance, so the TF-199 and TF-200 dates from the earlier Phase B are listed beside Possehl and Raval's Rojdi B dates without equating them. Within Rojdi B, PRL-1281 and PRL-1282 calibrate to 2015-1710 and 2000-1665 B.C. in Possehl and Raval's own table, inside their Rojdi C range rather than their Rojdi B range of 2200-2000 B.C. Mandal rejects TF-199 and TF-200 as stratigraphically inverted. Possehl and Raval reprint several PRL ages and sigmas slightly differently from the laboratory list (PRL-1083, PRL-1084, PRL-1088), and TF-199 with a sigma of 110 where TF-III prints 100. Kanungo and colleagues end Rojdi B at 1900 BCE instead of 2000 B.C. In Possehl and Raval's scheme the enclosure belongs to the early Post-urban, not to the Urban Phase.

parts.layout_phase: Period I, Phase A (Pandya and Nanavati)
parts.what_was_built: The first settlers 'built a 2-ft. high mud platform, capped by rammed earth and lime, to carry their mud and mud-brick houses' (IAR 1958-59, p. 19); in 1962-63 the Phase A 'mud-platform was found to support a succession of seven lime-floorings alternated with mud-ramming' (IAR 1962-63, p. 8). This is a house platform in the excavated part of the main mound, not a planned layout; Phase B followed 'after the destruction of the previous Phase by fire' with rubble and mud structures (IAR 1958-59, p. 19).
parts.excavator_basis: The 1957-63 excavators published no date for Phase A; the two radiocarbon dates of 1962-63 are from Phase B (IAR 1962-63, p. 8; Mandal 1972, p. 66). The radiocarbon entries below are the lower-level Main Mound dates of the 1982-86 excavation, which Possehl and Raval assign to Rojdi A (2500-2200 B.C., p. 171); that this Rojdi A is the same horizon as the earlier Phase A platform is our assumption, not a published statement.

first_occupation.phase: Rojdi A (Possehl and Raval); Period I, Phase A of the 1957-63 excavations
first_occupation.basis: Calibrated radiocarbon with the ceramic sequence: 'Rojdi A: 2500-2200 B.C.' (p. 171), with 'Average for Lowest levels: 2469 B.C.' for Trench 45K (p. 12, Table 2). Table 35 places Architectural Subphase 1a (a floor in 45K and a hearth in 46L) directly on virgin soil. Rojdi A pottery is 'quite similar to the pottery of Rangpur IIA' (p. 12).

notes: Rojdi, on the Bhadar river in Rajkot district, was excavated by P. P. Pandya in 1957-59, by J. M. Nanavati of the Gujarat State Department of Archaeology in 1962-63, and by M. H. Raval and G. L. Possehl in 1982-86. We record two parts. The planned element that matters for the town table is the boulder circumvallation with its gateway, which Possehl and Raval date by its pottery to Rojdi C, the early Post-urban phase, together with the main architectural period on the Main Mound and the South Extension; it is not a Mature Harappan layout. The second part is the house platform that the earlier excavators found under the first settlement, recorded so that the earliest built level has its dates beside it. Radiocarbon: the Physical Research Laboratory published fourteen Rojdi determinations in PRL-VI without context or phase; Possehl and Raval give trench, level and phase for twelve of them, on the 5568-year half-life with a 5730-based B.C. column and calibrated ranges. Their 5568 column for Rojdi matches the laboratory list, which confirms that the different-looking Lothal ages in their Table 1 are 5730-based. Two PRL-VI numbers are absent from Possehl and Raval: PRL-1091 (listed here with the Phase A part) and PRL-1081, 2360 ± 210 BP at 46-52 cm, which we leave out as probably later. Rojdi A dates are listed only with the platform part, and the circumvallation part carries the Rojdi C date and the Rojdi B and Phase B dates of the phase immediately before. We found no Bayesian model for Rojdi. Statements of wall direction in these sources were not recorded.
